title: The Awesome Leh
subtitle: 15 days, two school friends, zero network and a lot of rum

content:
Cheers, we said in Mocoholic for the chilled beer.

It was me and my school friend Mani.

It had been so many days since we had met and we were popping all the school time memories we had

Why don’t we go on a trip? He shot

Well, How about Leh, Ladakh? I’m anyway planning to go.

with? He asked

Not yet asked anyone. I just have a plan. I said

Okay. finalize the plan and let me know I will talk to my parents. He ended gulping beer.

This is so irritating, he said sliding his hands on the DSLR with the lens facing towards me.

What’s irritating? taking my pictures? I never asked you to take one. I mocked at him

No, Not taking your pictures, I meant about waiting for our next flight.

we were having a layover in Delhi to catch the flight to Leh.

We took the flight at 5 am and reached Leh around 7:30 A short guy holding board which had the full name of my friend and a shortened name of me was looking for us.
We met him and headed towards our stay.

Those who had not been there would have wondered what is actually Leh and what is Ladakh. Leh is a district out there and the region in which it is located is called Ladakh.
Ladakh, name sounds solid, isn’t it?

The Leh is totally encircled with military forces since it is close to Kargil and Pakistan. And every guy’s dream is to visit this place at least once in their lifetime. Well, it reaches your expectation as well. Perfectly suited weather can drive you crazy. It was the end of July, scorching sun and had got to know that was the summer then just for a week.

What crap, we have summers for months together sweating badly every time we step out.

On the first day, we were left for acclimatization in order to adjust ourselves in the high altitudes. Oxygen level will be too low and I was not able to reach the second floor without resting for 10 seconds on the first floor. Lavish room with wooden flooring which used to be super hot at day and super cold during the night times. What’s wrong with my phone? No calls no messages I thought to check it out and Man, No network!

I immediately switched on my other phone which I had carried with me purchasing a BSNL sim since somebody had told me except BSNL no other network sim works there. But even that’s not working.
What crap? I quickly freshened up and got connected with hotels wifi at reception.
Barely with one dot of strength, I was able to update my parents about my safe arrival and so did my friend.

I walked, walked and walked for 30minutes in the scorching sun and found the BSNL Office. Only postpaid sim works here sir, no prepaid. Yours is prepaid. Said the madam at bsnl Office. I scolded every person out there who had told me bsnl sim works here.
Couldn’t they tell me it should be postpaid?

Finally purchasing one local Aircel sim which would reach out to towers within 20kms circumference
of the Leh city head back to the stay. This entire thing took me 4 long hours and it was 2 pm when I reached back.

Having lunch I struggled myself to sleep despite tiredness since I had my bloody best Friend next to me.

The second day was way too usual despite our excitement to discover the snowy adventurous place of Ladakh.

Nice quote young man

Seemingly 65 years man said so pointing out to my Tee I looked out myself as in what it was written.

It said, “Nobody is too ugly after a few pegs of alcohol.”

Whattt? Didn’t my mom notice this?

Well, I would say no because she would have questioned me iThanks, Uncle, I said getting near him. we gently shook our hands and he introduced himself politely saying

Joseph Matthew here, Retired Brigadier of Indian Army.

I’m excited and in fact felt good for having him in my team there.

An extremely affectionate couple just boomed out of nowhere and started complimenting themselves.

Paldan mera naam, said the driver quickly glancing at our faces and turning back towards the road.

The very first place for the day was
Druk White Lotus School is known as 3-idiots school
Yes, the name says all. It is the school where Amir Khan ends up at the climax in 3-idiots movie.

On arrival here, you will be taken inside the campus with a guide and can visit different parts of the school.
Entering the premises enacting like typical HBO channel photographers, I and my friend took out DSLR and started to take pictures.

Bhaisab, band karo Padnekeliya nayi ata hai ?

We quickly wrapped everything inside and she left.

I immediately took out again put that to video mode and hung it on my shoulders opening the shutter cap.
It captured full video of school and children without anyone’s notice.

It has one wall painted with 3-idiot’s posters where you’re allowed to take pictures there. People posed in all possible ways :)

There is a café and one souvenir shop available inside the campus where you could see hanging Amir Khan and other cast’s pictures on the wall.
We had some good coffee at the souvenir shop with Paras and Aashitha.

The next place where we had reached was Hemis Monastery

It was around 50km drive from the place where we had stayed.

Hemis Monastery

The arch of the entrance has 8 unique symbols which were considered as lucky symbols for Buddhists. As we entered inside the archway climbing few tens of steps we could see beautiful quadrangle surrounded by 3 wide buildings on either side and the other with the stairways.

I was a little excited about getting to know a few aspects of Buddhism. I visited every temple in there wherein I could see calm, more decorated Gods. The Goddess was most likely depicting Goddess Kali Mata. Some of them are really peaceful which would make one meditate

over there and few most likely ferocious as said.

There is a small gallery there where we could get to know about Buddhism, their Gods, and worships, their drupka style, etc.

we straight away headed toThiksey Monastery

Thiksey Monastery

A splendid more beautiful monastery than Hemis. It is situated right from the bottom of foothill extending up to uphill.we could not trek till there in the scorching sun, There was a restaurant downhill, having lunch right there we asked driver Paldan to take us there in the car.

As said it is located on the uphill and never in my life, I had observed such a beautiful view out there from the temple terrace.I quickly went into the thoughts there.

Spending not much time we 6 people took few selfies and headed to Shanti Stupa

Shanti Stupa


It was en route Leh. It is a white-domed stupa (chorten) built by Japanese Buddhists and which has a lot of intuit things there. It says a lot about Mahapari Nirvana which means life after the death and how to attain nirvana.

The stupa has various phases of life from birth to death depicting it with symbols on the sides of the stupa. You would find them if you go around it. The turning wheel of dharma says a lot about Buddhist dharma and I barely could make out what those symbols there. Finally while stepping down the hill, there is a meditation hall where you could see the continuous beating of drums.

I entered in there and wondered what made me meditate for such a long time after opening my eyes after 20 minutes. I barely meditate and there; despite drum beats, I was not sure but I felt being positive there. We soon had a hot bowl of Maggi with red bull kind of energy drink which was made out of apricot and apple and ended our day.

we were back to Leh and supposed to be relaxing, wherein usually do not do when I go on to new places.

I went to Mall Road where usually every city in Himachal has it.

All shops piled in one single street where it will be the most happening place for tourists.

It was 1km from my place. I wanted to buy a good novel and my journey will always be incomplete without a novel. I had forgotten to carry it in hurries so went in search of that.

There was a lot of bookstores with a coffee shop. Best thing isn’t it?

Yes. it is the best I could find in Leh

Sip your coffee and enjoy reading.

Also, Leh is totally a foreigners place. Mostly foreigners rather than Indians there and that’s the main reason for having that culture of book reading with coffee. I quickly purchased One Indian girl authored by Chetan Bhagat despite looking for Oath of Vayuputras which I thought of buying and went back to hotel grabbing beers.

Beers and novel?
No, A novel is for journey and beer is to chill.

I should have rather preferred whiskey over beer for that cold weather. The night would be freaking cold. I use to feel bad if had to pee or shit we can’t wash our ass with the cold water that flows out of tap there.

Forget about washing ass, we were not able to put barefoot on the floor. Such cold

I was so done with that fluctuating weather.

Next day soon after the breakfast we were left to a place called Nubra valley.

Nubra valley

Nubra is like, I can say a most chilled place out there. It is around 160kms from the heart of the Leh, said travel guide Faraz

With no clue about the place, we got into SUV greeting to Paldan and to the rest. By then we all got closer just for a day itself. As the journey started, Mani started to chew Matthew uncles brain asking questions. He had served as the commando in the Kargil region a couple of decades back so he was enquiring about geographical topics.

I was laughing inside since he was the one who always scored less in history back in high school. But talented though. We had just crossed 10kms and god I felt like someone’s hitting my ass with stones. So worse are the roads there. Not able to sit properly for two minutes.

Left to right and vice versa was our movements.

Since that was our first day, we were restless and we got used to it later on. Roads in there are usually stony, you would find 5–10kms of a good road which would last in 15–20minutes and next 30–40kms will be stony ones which will last for 1.5hours to 2hours.

After traveling for about 4hours driver stopped at a place where the mountains are fully covered with snow and nothing is bare there.
Everything is covered with snow.

I quickly got down since I was waiting for something like this and then read the board Khardung La

Khardung La

That’s the highest motorable pass.

t the altitude of 18380ft and the most chilled place, I had experienced till then in the region of Leh.

I could not literally stand there for more than 10 minutes due to improper acclimatization. Within no time clicking pictures, my heart started being heavy and I got into vehicle and back to normal only after half an hour inhaling a small can of oxygen and resting for 15 minutes.

So I stepped down after that and after clicking couple more pictures having hot Maggie

we left to San Dunes at Hunder

After continuing our stony road journey for 3 more hours,

Almost like Rajasthan, Isn’t it? I asked myself stepping down of the vehicle seeing those deserted camels with their take carers, with such stunning landscapes against the backdrop of the snow-clad mountains, the Hunder Sand Dune looks nothing less than a fairy world.

Beyond its beauty, the dunes are home to the Bactrian Camels.

We had a couple more friends there, one was a Europian lady and the other one from Delhi who was close to us from the gang of make my trip.

we all four quickly went for ride sipping every little moment of the view out there. Words actually fell short to describe the blackish mountain view amidst of sand and dunes.

We continued our ride towards the Nubra putting a pit stop for lunch where we had a complimentary ATV Ride in mini desert kind of place, continuing to travel further, we reached the Diskit Monastery.

Maithreya Buddha at Diskit Monastery

Nothing much to describe this place except a 32-meter statue of Maitreya Buddha where one would remain silent and enjoy the blissfulness of the divinity there.

Since it was a very good attitude, the scenic was never the less enjoyable.
Finishing all these events by the time of 5 around, we reached our stay

The board hung at the gate said Himalayan desert stay.

Full lush green contradicting the word desert in its name with a big pond and White medium sized tents tightened to the four big hooks on the banks of a small pond. A spacious lawn at one corner of the pond allowing us to fire camp and activities

There were few more people from other places who were on the MakeMyTrip package. We all had bought good amounts of whiskey and rum. Keeping everything around the table which occupied most space in there we started to enjoy the campfire.

Everyone here is couples. Mani said

So? I said sipping rum over the stones

Ass, how weird is that only we both being here. He said

laughing hard I said, they are the wrong place man

Leh is for youth anyways forget about your feelings now and look at those two girls there, I said making an eye towards the two girls who were sitting opposite to us.

Do you know them? He asked

They are from Pune, though I’m not sure with the name. I said

You’re a good stalker no? He mocked.

Forget about that. See they are sitting naive in the midst of couples.

Let’s go talk to them? I said

We finished our alcohol, had dinner and started playing table tennis.

The European lady with Delhi based guy was there too with whom we were close with. The lady’s skills of playing table tennis were out of my imagination. We all played till 1 am and went back to the sleep. Next day was nothing much, we drove back to Leh. As usual, since we had reached early

Me, Mani, Paras, Ashitha had been to café in Mall Road.

Ashitha had made a friend with a girl out there in that café and we use to be their daily customers for one week having enough snacks with few complimentary from her.

The fifth day we left to Pangong

I had no idea of that place until I went there with stony road journey for about 7 hours. After seeing scooters similar to 3-idiots movie, I kind of startled why these people are such specimens, mounting solid scooters and taking pictures without a reason.

Got hit hard on my back.

Come to take my pictures. I will pose on the scooter like Kareena. Mani said

Kareena? What Kareena Kapoor?

Aye macha, where Kareena rides a yellow scooter in a bridal costume, to confess her love for Rancho

I laughed at my stupidity for not recognising.

Pangong Tso

It is the largest lake which extends up to China and yeah water will be so fucking cold you cannot step into it. You could spend hours in contemplation here, and still not have enough of its beauty. It is also known to change colors, appearing blue, green and red at different times and one should not miss visiting this place if they are making an expedition to Leh.

we finished all photo sessions except one at the stone in the water at some distance and a lake was shit cold. I was totally done with coldness there.

But without any option pulled my pants up and ran across to reach the stone at a 60mts distance to pose for one last picture there.

we drove on the sides of the lake to reach our stay. I was wondering where were the hotels there to stay.

Tents rugged up on the unlevelled floor with a kitchen in one corner with a good music system.
Our entire team was split into two and we had met new people this time than boring couples from the previous time. They were all in different tent stays.

Me mani we’re almost used to get in close with every guy out there.
Few ladies too especially the European lady with whom mani was flirting a lot despite her uncle boyfriend. There were other two couples from Mumbai where they were not at all like stereotypical couples.

We almost dosed on rum that night and started to dance like anything there. We were like 11 people boozing continuously, throwing mockeries at everyone else out there with no thought that we barely knew each other. Together all, finished 7 bottles of rum and started to dance.

Tents in Pangong Tso
Right in front of us at a distance of 100mts, Pangong lake reflecting grey, fire camp at the middle of us with emptied bottles of rum and whiskey
What else could I ask for?

I was tripped to the next level that day.

After all, I and Mani had a very good time recalling all our high school stack of memories we had made.

With a bad headache, we got up on the next day wherein we had to leave back to Leh. That was almost end of our Leh Ladakh journey.

The last day was meant to Leh city sightseeing wherein we had been to Leh Palace and other so not interested monasteries.

We all headed to Kargil War Memorial with Matthew uncle since he was from Indian Army we felt like going along with him.

Evoking a feeling of nationalism and patriotism at one glance, Kargil war memorial is a must visit attraction in Leh. The memorial is built to honor the soldiers who fought bravely in the Kargil war against Pakistan.
At the memorial house, one can see a picture description of the major event that took place during the war and army personals who lost their lives. Additionally, the memorial has a sandstone wall where the name of all the soldiers is inscribed. You can also purchase a few souvenirs there where the profit would go to the Indian Army.

Shopping a Kashmiri shawl for my mother, we wrapped the most amazing trip.

We had bid bye to all our gang there as it was their last day out there and since we were on the customized trip from MakeMyTrip, we departed to Manali from there.

The journey from Leh to Manali is not at all preferred and especially in local Tempo Travellers. I would suggest you book a government bus which departs Leh at 5 am in the morning, reaching Manali in the afternoon the next day.

We got on the bus early in the morning to Manali.

God the worsening of a road was to the next level. It was 36 hours of journey and I was already shit bored of the One Indian girl novel wherein I never had read such bad novel ever before.
The too dramatic and self-dominating story which I totally hated it and dropped in some hotel half way during the journey.

During the entire stretch of that journey, all I could remember is me falling up and down because of a road and having three plates of hot Maggi for lunch. Totally freaked out and was halted for the day at a place called Keylong.

We were asked to rest in a dormitory where we met another couple Sagar and Rachana They were based in Mumbai and had come to Leh for trekking expedition from a youth hostel

We four were in one dormitory and we had a good chat sharing our experiences about the journey.

The next day we left to Manali

Not sure with the distance left but trust me guys, the most beautiful stretch.

Whatever the pain in my ass I had for traveling to Keylong from Leh is all vanished just by the scenic I had the next day.

Lush green with tall trees spread across the mountainsides.
At least one small waterfall at one corner of mountain goes indescribable.

We reached Rohtang pass the most tagged place in social media by the persons who visit Manali.
Having groundnuts with tea and continued towards Manali We reached a place called Gulaba.

Passing Kothi valley where all the snow activities take place and I wasn’t exited much than my friend as this was my second visit there.

13kms traveling down the hill for about 4.5 hours with no hope of reaching foothill.

Yes, the previous time when I had been there we were lost on our hopes of being alive when we were stuck in snowfall.
A chill ran down my spine recalling those.
In fact, we hired same bikes this time in Manali, whichever two bikes we had hired before, But I totally missed my pals there.

We wrapped up our 15-day vacations covering Manali, Kasol, smoking high out there and roaming a bit around Delhi.

But I cannot miss mentioning aboutKasol

Kasol is again one heck of a place wherein it is situated at the banks of Parvati River and I bet nobody ever could have had a most tripping stay there than us.

We had stayed in the place called Alpine Guesthouse which is right in front of the river and those two days, I can hear nothing except the Parvati river sound.

Forget about cannabis, I never prefer tobacco as well but the quality and essence of the cannabis there made me trip back to back for about 12 hours.

Few Memories from the trip

▶ Watch Nubra Valley on YouTube

▶ Watch Pangong Lake on YouTube

places.name: Pangong
places.why: The largest lake that stretches into China, changing colours through the day — you simply cannot miss it.

places.name: Tsomoriri and Tsokar Lake
places.why: We missed it because of bad weather — and usually no package tour covers it since it involves extra permits and other headaches.

items: Only postpaid SIMs work in Leh — prepaid BSNL will not, so don't believe everyone.
A local Aircel-type SIM only reaches towers within about 20km of Leh city.
Give day one fully to acclimatization; even climbing to the second floor leaves you breathless.
Carry a small oxygen can for Khardung La — 18,380ft hits hard.
Expect stony roads: 5–10km of good road, then 30–40km of bone-rattling stretch.
Nights are freezing — carry whiskey over beer, and warm socks for the floor.
For Leh to Manali, book the 5am government bus instead of a local Tempo Traveller.
Carry a novel for the 36-hour road journey — just pick a better one than I did.
